transcript.text: My Shark cordless battery got really hot on charge last night and this morning it looks puffed up, the plastic case has split at the seam a bit. Can I still use it till a new one comes? It's the IZ201UK.

No — do not use, charge, or fit that battery back into the IZ201UK. A battery that became very hot and has swollen/split is damaged and can fail, vent flammable fumes, or catch fire.

What to do now:

• Unplug the charger from the wall and keep the battery away from the vacuum and charger.
• If it is still warm, smoking, hissing, smelling sweet/solvent-like, or leaking: do not handle it unnecessarily. Keep people and pets away and, if safe to do so, isolate it in a clear, well-ventilated area away from anything flammable (not on carpet, furniture, paper, etc.).
• Do not puncture, crush, open, tape tightly, put it in water, freeze it, or put it in a sealed container.
• Do not put it in household rubbish or normal recycling, and don’t post it back.
• Contact Shark UK support for a replacement and their instructions for a damaged/swollen battery. Also ask your local council household-waste/recycling centre whether they accept damaged lithium-ion batteries; tell them it is swollen, as it may need special handling.

If it starts smoking, flames appear, or you cannot safely isolate it, move away, warn others, and call 999. Do not try to continue using it “until the new one arrives” — use the vacuum only once you have an undamaged, compatible replacement battery.
